problem: The truelist/falselist rule and explanation are wrong. It says to backpatch E1.truelist to E2 so a false E1 jumps past E2, and gives truelist = merge(E1.truelist, E2.truelist), falselist = E2.falselist. For short-circuit &&, true jumps of E1 must go to the start of E2; overall truelist is E2.truelist; overall falselist is merge(E1.falselist, E2.falselist).
fix: For E1 && E2: backpatch(E1.truelist, start of E2); E.truelist = E2.truelist; E.falselist = merge(E1.falselist, E2.falselist). A true E1 continues to E2; a false E1 joins the false exits.

problem: The mirror rule is also stated incorrectly. It says keep E1.truelist and merge the two falselists. For short-circuit ||, a false E1 goes to E2, a true E1 is a true exit, and E2's true exits are also true exits. The overall falselist should be E2.falselist.
fix: For E1 || E2: backpatch(E1.falselist, start of E2); E.truelist = merge(E1.truelist, E2.truelist); E.falselist = E2.falselist.

problem: After combining a < b && c > d, the falselist is given as {103}. It must also contain the false jump from E1, instruction 101. The correct falselist is {101, 103}.
The final code is missing instructions 101 and 102, and instruction 100 is shown jumping to 104. That would skip the c > d test when a < b is true, so the code is not the short-circuit if-else.
The condition is printed as 'if (a  d)' and 'E1 = a  d', with the operators missing. The intended condition is if (a < b && c > d), with E1 = a < b and E2 = c > d.
fix: Translate if (a < b && c > d) x = 1; else x = 0; ... E1 = a < b, E2 = c > d.

problem: The bullet order omits emitting S1 before the end-of-then goto. As written, a student may emit the goto immediately after B and put S1 after the goto.
fix: After backpatching B.truelist to the start of S1, emit S1; then emit the blank goto; then backpatch B.falselist to the start of S2 and emit S2.

problem: M.instr is called an inherited attribute. In the standard marker-nonterminal construction, M -> ε sets M.instr = nextinstr, so M.instr is a synthesized attribute, not inherited.
fix: M carries one synthesized attribute, M.instr = nextinstr.

problem: The last sentence is false in general. For a non-nested procedure, the static link points to the enclosing (usually global) scope record, not necessarily to the caller's record. It equals the control link only when the caller is that same enclosing scope. In languages without nested procedures the static link may be omitted.
fix: Control link: caller's record, used for return/dynamic chain. Static link: record of the lexically enclosing scope, used for non-local access. For a non-nested procedure the static link points to the global/enclosing-scope record, and need not equal the control link.
